# Integrated native Scene fixtures

These fixtures are generated by this repository's
[generate_scene.py](../generate_scene.py), not contributed assets or copied
Blender source. They are redistributable test data under the repository's
[license](../../../LICENSE). Blender runs only as a separate generation and
verification process; native CTests do not require it.

## Provenance

Generated and verified on Windows on 2026-10-04:

| File | Blender build | Bytes | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `blender-4.5.13/scene.blend` | 4.5.13 LTS, `daeeeca98fb0` | 406267 | `b46bb22e1d5c4c8747971cac1f57aa6c58e737a9d48f00a948461446c43adfc8` |
| `blender-5.2.2/scene.blend` | 5.2.2 LTS, `d13f752e3b9c` | 524878 | `279ee61a35f9275870d441e7496b04a268361cc07bdd36e8cb060eb2970d998f` |

Both are uncompressed normal-save files. The active `Integrated` Scene has
source unit scale `0.01`, seven selected Objects and two unique selected
Mesh datablocks. An `Unselected` Scene contains an additional Mesh Object
that parents a selected Object but does not join selected membership.
File-browser directories are normalized to `//`; neither file contains
Windows absolute-path strings.

## Cases

- `Root` is a render-hidden Empty parenting the visible `MeshParent`.
- `MeshParent`, `SharedChild` and root Object `SharedRoot` share
  `SharedGeometry`, regardless of their different world transforms.
- Empty `mesh` is a child of `MeshParent`, and parents render-hidden
  `SharedChild`, forming a four-level mixed Mesh/Empty hierarchy. Its native
  identifier is `mesh_1`, reserving the Mesh parent's fixed `mesh` child.
- `EmptyRoot` is another data-less root.
- `Independent` uses `IndependentGeometry` and is parented to
  `OutsideParent` in the unselected Scene. That parent's distinct transform
  affects the child's world matrix; its `ParentOnlyGeometry` is not published.
- A nested Collection holds several Objects and shares `MeshParent` with
  the master Collection; selected membership must deduplicate it.
- Source transforms include delta channels, rotations, nonuniform and
  negative scales, and sheared parent inverse matrices.
- Each selected Mesh has five points, a quad and a triangle, seven corners,
  mixed smooth/flat normals and two UV maps. `Detail` deduplicates to five UV
  values; non-first render map `Render` retains seven values, including a
  seam and coordinates outside `[0, 1]`. The two Meshes differ in geometry.

## Oracle and checks

Adjacent `scene.oracle.txt` files use `BLEND_SCENE_ORACLE 1`, followed by
Blender's version string and the saved source unit scale, Object count and
unique Mesh count. Objects are in name order: each `OBJECT` record contains
quoted Object, saved parent and Mesh names, plus the Object's own render bit.
`WORLD` and `LOCAL` records contain 16 row-major source-basis matrix values.
Unique `MESH` records are in Mesh-name order and carry point, face, corner
and UV-map counts, followed by `POINT`, `COUNTS`, `INDICES`, `NORMAL`, `UV`
and per-corner `VALUE` records. Geometry comes directly from saved Mesh
datablocks, not transformed Object points or evaluated geometry.

Generation compares the oracle again after reopening the file.
`--check` first regenerates into a temporary directory, compares semantic
oracles, then reopens and checks the stored file without rewriting the
fixture or oracle. Matrices, points and normals use
`math.isclose(rel_tol=2e-6, abs_tol=2e-6)`; UV coordinates are exact, including
zero signs, as are names, references, flags, counts and topology.
Saved addresses and UI state are not byte-reproducible.
[test_generate_scene.py](../test_generate_scene.py) checks independent-process
and different-path reproduction, non-destructive success and failure,
home-path exclusion, modified-oracle rejection, and saved transform,
Mesh-sharing and UV mutations.

[SceneFixtureTests.cpp](../../../libs/blendScene/tests/SceneFixtureTests.cpp)
implements `blendScene.sceneFixture`. It independently reads unchanged
4.5.13 CustomData and 5.2.2 Attribute storage, selects the active Scene and
compares the owning IR after reader inputs have been released. It checks
selected parent indices, shared Mesh indices, membership deduplication,
parent-only exclusion, render bits and fixed-child naming. One source-unit
and basis conversion supplies expected points and world/local transforms;
normals are only basis-rotated and UVs remain unchanged. Matrices and points
use `2e-5 * (1 + abs(expected))` per component; normals use `2e-5`;
topology and expanded indexed UVs are exact. Oracle matrix homogeneous rows
must be within `1e-6` of affine before canonicalization; native validation
remains exact. Repeated loads and reversed block records must preserve all
metadata, Object/mesh order, graph indices, matrices and Mesh/UV arrays exactly.

Generation, check and regression commands are in the
[build guide](../../../docs/guides/building.md#integrated-scene-oracles).
The registered-plugin `test_stage.py` now compares the same oracles to
USD world/local transforms, hierarchy, visibility, points, topology, normals
and expanded UVs. Shared Meshes author distinct Mesh children and parent-only
Objects do not enter the stage. This remains fixed-scale integration evidence;
STAGE-O1's multi-scale evidence is recorded separately.
Current capability and incomplete milestone scope remain in the
[capability matrix](../../../docs/reference/CAPABILITY_MATRIX.md#5-scene-ir)
and [roadmap](../../../docs/roadmap/current.md).

## Unsupported-data fallback oracle

`blender-5.2.2/fallbacks.blend` is a separate, uncompressed normal-save
fixture generated and reopened on Windows on 2026-10-05 by
[generate_fallbacks.py](../generate_fallbacks.py), using Blender 5.2.2 LTS
build `d13f752e3b9c`. It has 540724 bytes and SHA-256
`dd65f2fecdaf78ee97217d0fecc212c7ab7023b9136bfe702defb7afb57b71e0`.
It is repository-generated, redistributable test data under the same license
as the integrated fixtures above; no Blender source or contributed assets
are included.

The active `Fallbacks` Scene extends the integrated fixture at unit scale
`0.01`, retaining 11 selected Objects and two unique Meshes:

- `Root` parents `CameraFallback`, then render-hidden `LightFallback`,
  then `TextFallback`, then the supported shared-Mesh Object `SharedRoot`.
- `ImageFallback` is an Image Empty parented to `MeshParent`.
- `OutsideParent` is now an unselected Camera parenting `Independent`;
  it shares Camera data with `CameraFallback` but never joins membership.
- The existing three shared-Mesh users, nested/shared Collection membership,
  render-hidden root/child, reflected/nonuniform transforms, sheared parent
  inverses, fixed-child reservation, topology, normals and indexed UVs remain.

The adjacent `fallbacks.oracle.txt` reuses `BLEND_SCENE_ORACLE 1` and the
matrix/geometry thresholds above. Non-Mesh records have no Mesh name; that
does not mean their source data is absent. Generation and checking explicitly
verify saved Camera/Light/text/Image source kinds and nonnull data, including
the parent-only Camera.

`blendScene.objectFallbacks` compares every owning IR value to the saved
oracle and requires exact repeated/reversed-block equality. It pins five
recoverable `Unsupported` `BLEND_SCENE_OBJECT_DATA_UNSUPPORTED` diagnostics,
each with the source Object name and exact payload offset/block index.
Shared unsupported data still reports each affected Object once.
`usdBlend.authoring` checks native-to-layer composition, stage hierarchy,
geometry, metadata-only output and deterministic repeated/reversed reads in
both build modes. Registered-plugin tests independently compare saved
world/local matrices, visibility and geometry, verify the same five warnings
in full and metadata-only reads, and retain reference/repeat behavior.

The fallback preserves Xforms, not Camera/Light schemas, text geometry or
Image data. Unmapped Object kinds, linked/invalid references, enabled
Collection instances and unsupported/invalid transforms remain fatal.
Other mapped kinds have synthetic fallback coverage only.
[test_generate_fallbacks.py](../test_generate_fallbacks.py) verifies
independent-process/path reproduction, home-path exclusion, non-destructive
checks and failures, modified-oracle rejection, removed Image data and
changed Camera transforms. Commands are in the
[build guide](../../../docs/guides/building.md#unsupported-data-fallback-oracle).
